Ingredients: 5 large bell peppers 12-16oz cream cheese 1 large package ground chorizo sausage 1 small block of cheddar or jack cheese 1 tablespoon of butter

Optional ingredients: Whole mushrooms White/red/green onions Bacon or uncooked bacon bits Spinach Any spicy seasoning

Directions: 1) cut a circle around the stem of each bell pepper. Grab the stem, twist, and pull. The seeds should come out with the stem. If there are any seeds left, pull them out. Then shake all the loose seeds out of the peppers. This step is important, because those seeds are spicy little fuckers that will get stuck in your gums, and nobody wants that. Set peppers aside for later use.

2) cut up any other vegetables you plan to use. Make sure they are diced very small, otherwise filling the peppers gets difficult. Take out the sausage and loosen it up so it will cook quickly and evenly, as well as to prevent big clumps of sausage from forming when it cooks.

3) grate approximately three large handfuls of the block of cheese into a large mixing bowl. Add in the cream cheese. Set aside for later use.

4) in a large sauce pan, melt the butter and coat the bottom of the pan by tilting it. Put the sausage in it, then follow with the vegetables at the appropriate times (put the ones with the longest cooking time in first).

5) pour the contents of the saucepan into the mixing bowl, and mix to an even consistency. The mixture should be an alarming orange colour that looks disgusting.

6) scoop a portion of the mixture into a gallon sized zip lock bag, and push it all into one corner. Cut the tip of the corner at a 45 degree angle, leaving an opening about a half inch wide. Squeeze mixture through the hole into the peppers. When the peppers appear full, use a spoon to pack in the filling mixture, and refill the peppers.

7) place peppers in an oven-safe dish. Fill the dish with water about an inch deep, then put in oven at 325 for 15-20 min. When ready, the peppers should bend inwards easily when you poke them. Remove dish from oven and serve. The peppers will not be too hot to touch (probably), but the filling will be.
